newsitem.title: USA: Dover sees slower earnings rise in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Dover sees slower earnings rise in 1997.

text.p: Dover Corp said Friday it expects earnings to rise in 1997, but at a slower rate than in recent years.

In 1996 the company earned $3.01 a share before gains from divestitures. These earnings were up 23 percent from 1995 on a nine percent increase in sales, Dover said. It was the smallest profit gain in four years.
It said the favorable impact in 1997 from acquisitions made last year was not likely to exceed $0.05 per share after acquisition premium write-off and financing costs.

Dover said the first quarter will probably show only a small increase. Belvac, Midland and the two Heil companies are now operating at levels well below their 1996 first quarter and do not expect favorable comparisons until later in 1997, it said.
Beyond the first quarter, Dover said, its earnings comparisons should be more favorable.
